Became interim president in January 1991 after Barry Thompson resigned and was inaugurated the 14th president in April 1992, serving until 2009; the leader in office in 1996 and anchor of the chain.

Served as TSU president 1991-2005 after seven years as president of Jackson State University; the leader in office in 1996 and anchor of the chain. Enrollment reached an all-time high during his tenure.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: TSU's seventh president, 2005-2011; came from the provostship at Winston-Salem State and had earlier held academic-affairs posts at North Carolina A&T. Announced his retirement in 2010.
Interim president from Jan. 2, 2011 to Dec. 31, 2012, the first woman to lead TSU; she had previously served as president of Albany State University (1996-2005).

leaders.nextRole: Retired (president emerita; international president of Alpha Kappa Alpha)
leaders.notes: TSU's eighth president and first female permanent president, Jan. 2, 2013 to June 30, 2024; she retired amid mounting financial and enrollment problems, with a contract buyout, on the eve of the university's governance crisis.

Appointed interim president July 1, 2024 for a one-year term after Glover retired, but resigned abruptly effective Dec. 13, 2024 (about 120 days in), citing a fundamental difference with the board. This came during TSU's 2023-2025 governance crisis, in which the Tennessee legislature vacated the university's board and Gov. Bill Lee appointed an entirely new board in 2024, and the university narrowly avoided insolvency.

Tennessee Tech's seventh president, 1987-2000; the leader in office in 1996 and anchor of the chain. He came from East Carolina University, where he had been VP for academic affairs, and grew the endowment from about $1 million to $27 million.

The university's eighth president, July 1, 2000 to 2012; an internal promotion, he had joined the Tech faculty in 1976 and served as business dean from 1991 to 2000, overseeing 11 straight years of enrollment growth as president.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Became Tennessee Tech's ninth president July 1, 2012, coming from the provostship at UT Chattanooga (a chemist who earlier chaired the department and was arts-and-sciences dean at Mississippi State). Still serving; no active presidential search.
